docs.title: VSUART: UART IP Documentation
docs.text: VSUART (Vietnamese Systemware UART) is a configurable UART IP with an APB4 slave interface, implemented in SystemVerilog. This documentation covers the peripheral interface, RTL architecture, and UVM 1.2 verification environment.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The IP provides separate transmit and receive paths with FIFO buffering, programmable baud generation, configurable frame formats, and TX, RX, and error interrupt outputs. Control and status registers are accessed through the APB interface.

The design separates the APB and UART clock domains. A programmable prescaler derives the internal UART clock from the system clock. See RTL architecture for the module structure and data paths.

docs.title: Organization of this documentation
docs.text: The documentation is organized into the following sections.

docs.title: Specification
docs.text:
The specification pages describe the externally visible behavior of the peripheral:

  • Features & frame formats: supported configurations, frame encoding, and the interactive frame explorer.
  • Interfaces & clocks: APB signals, serial ports, resets, and clock requirements.
  • Register map: offsets, fields, reset values, and access policies.
  • Clock & baud rate: timing equations, reference configurations, and the baud rate calculator.
  • UART operation: configuration, enable sequencing, transmission, and reception.
  • Interrupts & errors: trigger selection, status flags, and interrupt servicing.

docs.title: RTL design
docs.text: The Architecture describes the APB subsystem, TX/RX engines, asynchronous FIFOs, clock-domain crossings, and top-level parameters. It combines the design document with implementation references from the local source tree.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: The UVM environment presents the environment diagram and component responsibilities. Tests lists the 23 scenarios from the verification test plan and their execution status.

docs.title: Key parameters
docs.text: Item Project specification Host interface APB4 slave; 16-bit address, 32-bit data, four byte strobes Serial data 8 bits with no, odd, or even parity; 9 bits with no parity Stop bits One or two RX oversampling 4× or 16× FIFO capacity Up to 128 entries; top-level default 128 × 9 bits Register bank Seven 32-bit CSRs at 0x0000–0x0018 FIFO data port 0xFFFF: write TX data or read RX data Interrupt outputs TX, RX, and error System clock 40–200 MHz APB clock At most 72 MHz; satisfy Fsys > Fpclk > Fu

docs.title: RTL architecture
docs.text:
VSUART separates bus access, serial transmission, and serial reception. A prescaler produces u_clk; asynchronous FIFOs and CDC logic move data, configuration, and status between clock domains.

This is a functional summary of the source structure. See the original block diagram in FunctionalSpec, Figure 1-1.

docs.title: APB, control, and status
docs.text: Module Responsibility vsuart_apb_slv Route APB accesses to the CSR bank or FIFO data port; generate responses vsuart_reg Implement MODE, CR, STA, PRS, BRG, IE, IFS, and write guards vsuart_ifs Generate interrupt outputs from flags and enables vsuart_prs Divide sys_clk into u_clk using PRS vsuart_sync_a2u Transfer configuration/control from APB to UART vsuart_sync_u2a Transfer status/events from UART to APB

docs.title: TX datapath
docs.text:
APB write @ 0xFFFF → TX asynchronous FIFO → parallel-to-serial shifter
                                               ↓
                         parity + controller + bit counter → TX generator → o_tx
  • vsuart_tx_brg generates transmit baud enables.
  • vsuart_tx_ctrl handles idle, start, data, parity, and stop states.
  • vsuart_tx_p2s_shifter serializes the payload.
  • vsuart_tx_parity generates parity when selected by the frame format.
  • vsuart_tx_gen selects the output line value for each frame phase.

The TX FIFO is an asc_fifo instance in the top module. It accepts APB-domain writes and supplies UART-domain reads. MODE selects the frame format.

docs.title: RX datapath
docs.text:
i_rx → start detector → sampled serial-to-parallel shifter → RX FIFO → APB read
                              ↓
                         parity/frame checker → status / error

vsuart_rx_start detects the start condition; vsuart_rx_brg controls sampling. The controller, bit counter, and vsuart_rx_s2p_shifter assemble data. vsuart_rx_checker checks parity and stop bits; vsuart_rx_fifo buffers received data and provides status.

docs.title: Clock-domain crossings
docs.text:
DesignSpec §1.2 records two changes to reused common modules:

  • Handshake-based CDC for transfers from a faster clock domain to a slower domain.
  • Additional character-count information in the asynchronous FIFO.

Shared RTL is under 0_rtl/common/, including cdc_unit, cdc_unit_hs, edge_det, bit_cnt, register primitives, and asc_fifo/.

FunctionalSpec requires Fsys > Fpclk > Fu. The presence of CDC modules describes structure; timing closure and CDC sign-off require separate evidence.

docs.title: Top-level parameters
docs.text:
vsuart parameter Default in 0_rtl/vsuart.v ADDR_W 16 DATA_W 32 FIFO_DEPTH 128 FIFO_DATA_W 9 STRB_W DATA_W / 8; source comment says not to override directly

vsuart_define.v also contains a FIFO_DEPTH=32 macro. The testbench instantiates the top without parameter overrides, so the top default applies to that instance. Check the elaborated parameters when integrating the IP.

Design document maturity

DesignSpec revision 0.01 contains an older hierarchy, repeated entries, and incomplete detailed sections. The module names above were checked against the RTL. Implementation descriptions supplement the PDF rather than quoting missing sections.

Sources: DesignSpec §1, PDF pp. 4–5, FunctionalSpec §1.2, PDF pp. 5–6, 0_rtl/vsuart.v, vsuart_tx.v, vsuart_rx.v, and vsuart_define.v.

docs.title: Clock & baud rate
docs.text: The prescaler derives u_clk from sys_clk. TX uses a bit enable at the baud rate; RX samples at OS times that rate.

docs.title: Timing equations
docs.text:
OS        = 16 when BSEL = 0; 4 when BSEL = 1
Fu        = Fsys / (2 × (PRS + 1))
BRG_ideal = Fu / (OS × target_baud) − 1
baud      = Fu / (OS × (BRG + 1))
Fsample   = Fu / (BRG + 1) = OS × baud
error (%) = 100 × (baud − target_baud) / target_baud

Allowed ranges: PRS=0…15, BRG=1…65535, system clock 40–200 MHz, and APB clock at most 72 MHz. The required ordering is Fsys > Fpclk > Fu. Program PRS only while UEN[2]=0.

docs.title: Baud rate calculator
docs.text:
Choose the prescaler and oversampling ratio. The calculator tests the two integers adjacent to BRG_ideal and selects the one with the smaller absolute baud error. Out-of-range targets are clamped to a valid divisor and clearly flagged. PRS is not selected automatically; review the error tolerance of the remote device.

System clock (MHz) APB clock (MHz) Prescaler · PRS (0–15) Oversampling16× · BSEL = 04× · BSEL = 1 Target baud rate (bit/s) Enable JavaScript to use the interactive calculator. The equations and worked example below remain available without JavaScript.

docs.title: Worked example from the specification
docs.text:
For Fsys=40 MHz, PRS=4, BSEL=1 (4×), and a target of 9,600 bit/s:

Quantity Result UART clock 40 MHz / (2 × 5) = 4 MHz Selected BRG 103 (0x0067) Actual baud 4,000,000 / (4 × 104) = 9,615.3846 bit/s RX sampling 4,000,000 / 104 = 38,461.5385 Hz Baud error +0.1603%

Choose an APB clock greater than 4 MHz and less than 40 MHz to satisfy the ordering. The PDF does not select a PCLK value for this example.

docs.text:

docs.title: Clock enables while idle
docs.text:
Section 4.2.2 generates tx_cken only while TX is enabled and transmitting; RX sampling enables are generated during reception with RX enabled. Derive frame timing from the actual divided baud rate rather than a rounded target.

Sources: FunctionalSpec §§3.5–3.6, PDF pp. 12–14, §4.2.2, PDF p. 17, and §5, PDF p. 21.

docs.title: Features & frame formats
docs.text: VSUART is a configurable serial transmitter and receiver controlled through an APB4 slave interface. The design separates the APB clock domain from the UART core; a prescaler derives u_clk from sys_clk.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
Capability Project specification Host interface APB4 slave with continuous read/write transactions Data width 8 or 9 bits Parity None, odd, or even for 8-bit data; none for 9-bit data Stop bits 1 or 2 Buffering TX/RX FIFOs up to 128 entries Timing Programmable prescaler and baud divisor; 4× or 16× oversampling Interrupts TX, RX, and error outputs; TX/RX triggers selected by CR RX checks Framing and parity error detection

Although the overview references 16550 functionality, VSUART defines its own register map. Software compatibility with a standard 16550 register layout should not be assumed.

docs.title: Choose a frame format
docs.text:
PDSEL[17:16] Data bits Parity Shorthand 00 8 None 8N 01 8 Odd 8O 10 8 Even 8E 11 9 None 9N

SPSEL=0 selects one stop bit; SPSEL=1 selects two. A frame begins with a low start bit. Data is transmitted least significant bit first, as implemented in vsuart_tx_p2s_shifter.v and checked by the TX basic test.

Idle → Start → D0 → D1 → D2 → D3 → D4 → D5 → D6 → D7 → Stop → Idle/Start
  1      0     LSB                                  MSB      1

An 8N1 frame occupies 10 bit-times. Eight data bits with parity and one stop bit occupy 11 bit-times, excluding any idle gap between frames. Try the interactive frame explorer to see the bits change.

docs.title: Frame explorer
docs.text:
Select a frame format and enter a hexadecimal payload to inspect the transmitted bits. The waveform is an illustrative frame, independent of baud timing or DUT simulation.

UART FRAME EXPLORERINTERACTIVE 8N18E19N2DATA 0x

Enter a hexadecimal payload (00–FF for 8-bit, 000–1FF for 9-bit).

StartDataParityStop8 data bits · No parity · 1 stop bit

Illustrative frame · 10 bit-times · LSB first

Enable JavaScript to explore frames. An 8N1 frame contains a low start bit, eight data bits sent LSB first, and a high stop bit: 10 bit-times in total.

docs.title: Enable and reset behavior
docs.text:
• UEN[2] enables the UART core and prescaler.
  • UEN[0] enables TX when UEN[2]=1.
  • UEN[1] enables RX when UEN[2]=1.
  • Disabling TX aborts transmission and resets its buffer.
  • Disabling RX resets its buffer.

Enable TX before writing payloads to its FIFO. Data written while TX is disabled should not be expected to survive until a later enable. Follow the operation sequence.

Line break support

FunctionalSpec §1.1 lists break generation and detection, but does not define a detailed control register or usage sequence. A software API for break is therefore still an open documentation item.

Sources: FunctionalSpec §1.1, PDF p. 4, §3.2, PDF pp. 9–10, and §4.1, PDF p. 16.

docs.title: Interfaces & clocks
docs.text: Signal names follow FunctionalSpec. The RTL column gives the corresponding port on 0_rtl/vsuart.v.

docs.title: Clock and reset
docs.text:
Specification RTL port Direction Description sys_clk sys_clk Input System clock, 40–200 MHz rst_n rst_n Input Asynchronous, active-low system and CSR reset PCLK pclk Input Rising-edge APB clock, at most 72 MHz PRESETn preset_n Input Active-low reset for the APB side

FunctionalSpec §5 requires Fsys > Fpclk > Fu. The internal prescaler generates u_clk; see the baud rate calculator for formulas and clock checks.

The current testbench connects both DUT resets to clk_rst_vif.rst_n. This is testbench wiring; an integration must determine its own reset connections.

docs.title: APB4 slave
docs.text: Signal RTL port Width Direction Purpose PADDR i_paddr 16 Input CSR offset or FIFO data address 0xFFFF PSEL i_psel 1 Input Select this peripheral PENABLE i_penable 1 Input APB ACCESS phase PWRITE i_pwrite 1 Input Write when high; read when low PWDATA i_pwdata 32 Input Write data PSTRB i_pstrb 4 Input Valid write byte lanes PREADY o_pready 1 Output Transfer completion; specification initial value 1 PRDATA o_prdata 32 Output Read data; initial value 0 PSLVERR o_pslverr 1 Output Access error; initial value 0

docs.title: CSR and FIFO accesses
docs.text:
Seven 32-bit CSRs occupy offsets 0x0000 through 0x0018.

  • TX write: PADDR=0xFFFF, payload in PWDATA[8:0], PSTRB=0011.
  • RX read: PADDR=0xFFFF, receive payload from PRDATA[8:0].
  • Data bits [31:9] are reserved for FIFO accesses.

Use the exact FIFO address

0xFFFF is a special data address defined by the project specification. Do not round it down to 0xFFFC in a bus sequence.

docs.title: Error conditions
docs.text:
Access Specified response Write BSEL, PDSEL, SPSEL, or BRG while the core is active and either TX or RX remains enabled Ignore the write and assert PSLVERR Write PRS while UEN[2]=1 Ignore the write and assert PSLVERR Read an empty RX FIFO Report a transfer error

The specification also requires TX and RX to be idle when changing CR or IE. Invalid software accesses are not necessarily blocked in hardware.

docs.title: Serial and interrupt ports
docs.text:
RTL port Direction Purpose i_rx Input Received serial data o_tx Output Transmitted serial data o_txifs Output TX interrupt o_rxifs Output RX interrupt o_errifs Output Error interrupt

Sources: FunctionalSpec §2, PDF pp. 7–8, §4.4, PDF pp. 18–20, §5, PDF p. 21, and 0_rtl/vsuart.v.

docs.title: Interrupts & errors
docs.text: VSUART exposes TX, RX, and error interrupts. CR selects trigger conditions, IE enables sources, and IFS holds flags. Software clears flags by writing one to the corresponding bits.

docs.title: TX trigger selection
docs.text:
TXISEL FunctionalSpec condition 00 A character moves from TX FIFO to the transmit shift register 01 All characters have been transmitted and transmission is complete 10 A character moves into the shift register and TX FIFO becomes empty 11 TX buffer overflow

FIFO empty and transmission complete are different events. In mode 10, the shift register may still be sending the final frame. Mode 01 describes completion of the entire transmission.

docs.title: RX trigger selection
docs.text: RXISEL FunctionalSpec condition 00 or 01 (0x) A character is received / buffer is nonempty 10 RX buffer reaches three-quarters capacity 11 RX buffer is full

docs.title: Receive error status
docs.text:
STA field Bit Meaning Specified clear FRERR 3 A received stop bit is low Read STA PRERR 4 Received parity does not match configuration Read STA RBOSTA 6 RX buffer overflow Read STA; RTL clear-mask discrepancy remains

Section 4.3 identifies framing and parity errors as sources of ERRIFS. The source does not clearly establish that every overflow generates an error interrupt.

docs.title: Service an interrupt
docs.text:
1. Read IFS to identify pending sources.
  2. For RX or error handling, read and save STA; this clears R1C flags under the specification.
  3. Transfer data through the FIFO as appropriate and check the APB response.
  4. Write a W1C mask to IFS for the serviced sources.
  5. Recheck flags if new events may have occurred during service.
Source IE enable IFS flag Clear mask TX TXTE[0] TXIFS[0] 0x00000001 RX RXTE[8] RXIFS[8] 0x00000100 Error ERRIE[16] ERRIFS[16] 0x00010000

Simultaneous set and clear

The specification gives APB clear priority over internal status or interrupt events. Verify simultaneous set/clear behavior explicitly. An unconditional read-modify-write on W1C flags can clear other pending sources unintentionally.

Sources: FunctionalSpec §§3.3–3.4, PDF pp. 11–12, §§3.7–3.8, PDF p. 15, and §4.3, PDF pp. 17–18.

docs.title: UART operation
docs.text: Configure the peripheral while it is disabled, then enable the required data paths. This sequence combines the register restrictions in FunctionalSpec §3 with the usage guidance in §4.

docs.title: Initial configuration
docs.text:
1. Reset the system and APB interface; verify clock and reset connections.
  2. Set MODE.UEN=000. Use PSTRB=0001 when changing only the enable field.
  3. Select PRS, BSEL, and BRG using the baud rate calculator. Check Fsys > Fpclk > Fu.
  4. Program PRS while the core/prescaler is disabled. Program BRG, PDSEL, SPSEL, and BSEL while UART is disabled.
  5. With both TX and RX idle, select CR.TXISEL/RXISEL and the interrupt enables in IE.
  6. Handle pending flags as required: reading STA has side effects; clear IFS using W1C masks.
  7. Enable the required paths: UEN=101 for TX, 110 for RX, or 111 for both.
  8. Read back the configuration and check PSLVERR on APB responses.

RX setup order

FunctionalSpec §4.4.2 lists RX enable before configuration. The sequence above follows the explicit restrictions in §3 by configuring first and enabling afterward.

docs.title: Transmit a character
docs.text:
Step Action Check enables UEN[2]=1 and UEN[0]=1 Check space Inspect TBSTA for a full buffer; remember that reading STA clears error flags Write payload PADDR=0xFFFF, PWRITE=1, PSTRB=0011, payload in PWDATA[8:0] Complete APB access Observe PREADY and check PSLVERR Observe TX The engine drains its FIFO using the selected frame format Detect completion TRSTA describes an empty shift register and buffer; TX interrupt mode 01 means all transmission is complete

In 8-bit mode, payload bit 8 is not transmitted as a data bit. The TX basic test checks this with randomized 9-bit APB payloads.

docs.title: Receive a character
docs.text:
1. Enable the core and RX (UEN[2]=1, UEN[1]=1) with a format matching the sender.
  2. Observe RBDSTA or the configured RX interrupt.
  3. Read PADDR=0xFFFF with PWRITE=0; take the payload from PRDATA[8:0].
  4. Check the APB error response. Reading an empty RX FIFO is an error.
  5. Read and save STA to handle FRERR, PRERR, and RBOSTA; clear the serviced IFS flags with W1C masks.

docs.title: Continuous transfers
docs.text:
FunctionalSpec illustrates back-to-back APB FIFO writes and reads. The TX basic test checks a SETUP phase followed by ACCESS for each item, permits ACCESS wait states, and requires PSEL to remain asserted across the burst.

  • APB FIFO write waveform, PDF p. 19
  • APB FIFO read waveform, PDF p. 20

docs.title: Disable or reconfigure
docs.text:
Wait for the relevant paths to become idle, disable TX/RX and the core, and update frame and clock parameters before enabling again. Disabling a path resets its buffer; disabling TX also aborts an in-progress transmission. Plan for pending data before disabling.

Source: FunctionalSpec §§3–4, PDF pp. 9–20.

docs.title: Register map
docs.text:
Seven 32-bit control/status registers configure VSUART. Offsets, access policies, and reset values below follow FunctionalSpec. Reserved bits read as zero and must not carry application data.

Check reset expectations

The specification and RAL reset IE to zero, while RTL defines 0x00010101. STA also differs across the specification, RTL POR macro, and RAL fields. Account for these differences when interpreting reset behavior.

docs.title: Register summary
docs.text:
Offset Register Specified reset Access Purpose 0x0000 MODE 0x00010000 RO/RW Enables, frame format, oversampling 0x0004 CR 0x00000000 RO/RW TX/RX interrupt selection 0x0008 STA 0x00000024 RO/R1C Status and errors 0x000C PRS 0x00000000 RO/RW UART clock prescaler 0x0010 BRG 0x00000001 RO/RW Baud divisor 0x0014 IE 0x00000000 RO/RW Interrupt enables 0x0018 IFS 0x00000000 RO/W1C Interrupt flags 0xFFFF FIFO data port — Write TX / Read RX Payload [8:0]; separate from the CSR bank

RW: read/write. RO: read only. R1C: a status read clears asserted flags. W1C: writing one clears the selected flag; writing zero leaves it unchanged.

docs.title: MODE · 0x0000
docs.text:
Bits Field Reset Access Meaning [2:0] UEN 000 RW Bit 0: TX; bit 1: RX; bit 2: core/prescaler [8] BSEL 0 RW 0: 16× oversampling; 1: 4× [17:16] PDSEL 01 RW 00: 8N; 01: 8O; 10: 8E; 11: 9N [24] SPSEL 0 RW 0: one stop bit; 1: two stop bits Other bits Reserved 0 RO —

Write BSEL, PDSEL, and SPSEL only when UEN[2]=0 or UEN[1:0]=00. A locked write is ignored and reports PSLVERR. When changing only enables, write byte 0 (PSTRB=0001) to avoid touching the frame/baud configuration bytes, as in the TestEnv uart_enable() helper.

docs.title: CR · 0x0004
docs.text:
Bits Field Reset Access [1:0] TXISEL 00 RW [9:8] RXISEL 00 RW Other bits Reserved 0 RO

TXISEL: 00 FIFO to shift register; 01 all transmission complete; 10 FIFO becomes empty as a character moves to the shift register; 11 TX buffer overflow.

RXISEL: 0x received character; 10 RX buffer three-quarters full; 11 RX buffer full. Change CR only with TISTA=1 and RISTA=1 under the specification. See interrupts.

docs.title: STA · 0x0008
docs.text:
Bit Field Specified reset Access Meaning when set 0 TBSTA 0 RO TX buffer full 1 TRSTA 0 RO TX shift register and buffer empty; transmission complete 2 TISTA 1 RO TX idle 3 FRERR 0 R1C Framing error 4 PRERR 0 R1C Parity error 5 RISTA 1 RO RX idle 6 RBOSTA 0 R1C RX buffer overflow 7 RBDSTA 0 RO RX buffer contains data [31:8] Reserved 0 RO —

A read has side effects

Under FunctionalSpec, reading STA clears asserted FRERR, PRERR, and RBOSTA. Save the returned value before handling errors. Polling or debugger reads may consume flags. The RTL clear mask currently includes only bits 3 and 4; verify RBOSTA separately.

The specification gives APB clear priority over internal status events.

docs.title: PRS · 0x000C
docs.text:
Bits Field Reset Access Range [3:0] PRS 0 RW 0–15 [31:4] Reserved 0 RO —

Fu = Fsys / (2 × (PRS + 1)). Write only while UEN[2]=0. Otherwise, the write is ignored and PSLVERR is asserted.

docs.title: BRG · 0x0010
docs.text:
Bits Field Reset Access Range [15:0] BRG 1 RW 1–65535 [31:16] Reserved 0 RO —

Baud = Fu / (OS × (BRG + 1)). The specification prohibits BRG=0 because it produces invalid RX sampling behavior. Write restrictions match the frame fields in MODE. Calculate a divisor →

docs.title: IE · 0x0014
docs.text:
Bit Field Specified reset Access Purpose 0 TXTE 0 RW TX interrupt enable 8 RXTE 0 RW RX interrupt enable 16 ERRIE 0 RW Error interrupt enable Other bits Reserved 0 RO —

Change IE while TX and RX are idle. Section 4.3 also uses the names TXIE/RXIE; this page follows the register table names in §3.7.

docs.title: IFS · 0x0018
docs.text:
Bit Field Reset Access 0 TXIFS 0 W1C 8 RXIFS 0 W1C 16 ERRIFS 0 W1C Other bits Reserved 0 RO

Clear TX with 0x00000001, RX with 0x00000100, or error with 0x00010000. Select the corresponding byte strobes. Avoid unconditional read-modify-write operations on W1C flags.

APB clear takes priority over internal interrupt events under the specification. Revision 0.04 removed VSUART_IFC; clear flags through IFS.

Sources: FunctionalSpec §3, PDF pp. 9–15 and TestEnv sheet 7, B25:C31.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
The 23 verification scenarios below follow sheet 3.Test_Scenario of the VSUART Testplan.

Status: PASS = passed; NOT RUN = not yet executed. The project owner confirmed PASS for the three scenarios with a finished date in the test plan. The remaining 20 scenarios have not yet been executed.

Summary: 23 testcases — 3 PASS, 20 NOT RUN.

docs.title: 1. vsuart_reset_value_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F1.1.3.1, F2.1.1.2 Method: Waveform + Self-check TM Priority: Medium

Verify register reset values after power-on reset and after rst_n assertion during operation.

Pass criteria: All registers equal their reset values after Power On Reset and after rst_n during operation; output pins are in the reset state.

docs.title: 2. vsuart_apb_reset_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F1.1.4.1, F1.1.4.2 Method: Waveform Priority: Medium

Verify APB slave recovery after PRESETn, including PRESETn in the middle of an APB transfer.

Pass criteria: APB returns to IDLE after every PRESETn; the interrupted transfer is not completed; following transfers complete without error and data_read = data_write.

docs.title: 3. vsuart_csr_rw_access_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.1.1.1, F2.1.1.3, F2.2.1.1 Method: Self-check TM + Assertion Priority: High

Verify register write/read-back with byte strobes, back-to-back APB transfers, RO and reserved bits.

Pass criteria: data_read = data_write on RW fields (per byte strobe); RO and reserved bits are not modified; no transfer is lost in back-to-back mode; PSLVERR=0.

docs.title: 4. vsuart_pslverr_locked_write_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.1.2.1 Method: Self-check TM Priority: Medium

Verify PSLVERR when protected registers are written while UART is enabled.

Pass criteria: Writes to protected registers while UART is enabled give PSLVERR=1 and do not change the register; the same writes with UART disabled are accepted (data_read = data_write).

docs.title: 5. vsuart_brg_range_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.3.1.1, F2.3.1.2 Method: Self-check TM Priority: Medium

Verify TX baud rate for the standard baud rates in 16x (BSEL=0) and 4x (BSEL=1) oversampling.

Pass criteria: Bit period = Oversample x (BRG+1) / Fu_clk with Fu_clk = Fsys_clk / (2 x (PRS+1)); transmitted data = written data.

docs.title: 6. vsuart_brg_boundary_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.3.2.1, F2.3.2.2, F2.3.2.3 Method: Self-check TM Priority: Medium

Verify baud rate generation at the BRG limits (BRG=1, BRG=65535) and with the illegal value BRG=0.

Pass criteria: Bit period = Oversample x (BRG+1) / Fu_clk for BRG=1 and BRG=65535; UART_BRG safely handles the illegal value BRG=0.

docs.title: 7. vsuart_tx_basic_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.1.3.1, F2.4.1.1, F2.4.2.1, F2.4.2.3 Method: Self-check TM Priority: High

Finished date in test plan: 26/10/29; Status: PASS (confirmed by the project owner).

Verify TX FIFO write via APB, the serial frame sequence on tx and back-to-back transmission.

Pass criteria: Transmitted data = written data, in the same order; frame sequence and bit time are correct; no gap between consecutive frames; APB signals follow the protocol.

docs.title: 8. vsuart_tx_frame_formats_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.4.2.2 Method: Self-check TM Priority: High

Finished date in test plan: 26/10/29; Status: PASS (confirmed by the project owner).

Verify transmission in all frame formats (8/9 data bits, none/even/odd parity, 1/2 stop bits).

Pass criteria: Data bits, parity bit and stop bits match the configured format; data bit 8 is kept in 9-bit mode; transmitted data = written data.

docs.title: 9. vsuart_tx_fifo_status_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.4.1.2, F2.4.1.3 Method: Self-check TM Priority: Medium

Verify TX FIFO status flags from empty through full and back to empty (TBSTA, TISTA, TRSTA).

Pass criteria: TBSTA shows FIFO full, TISTA shows TX idle, TRSTA is 1 only when TX FIFO and shift register are empty; transmitted data = written data, in the same order.

docs.title: 10. vsuart_tx_fifo_overflow_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.4.1.4, F2.4.4.4 Method: Self-check TM + Assertion Priority: Medium

Verify TX FIFO overflow: the extra character is dropped and TXIFS is set (TXISEL=2'b11).

Pass criteria: The 129th character is dropped; the 128 accepted characters are transmitted in order (transmitted data = written data); TXIFS is set on overflow and cleared by writing 1.

docs.title: 11. vsuart_tx_irq_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.4.4.1, F2.4.4.2, F2.4.4.3 Method: Assertion + Self-check TM Priority: Medium

Verify TX interrupt generation for TXISEL=2'b00, 2'b10 and 2'b01.

Pass criteria: TXIFS and ifs_tx assert at the event selected by TXISEL and de-assert after writing 1 to IFS[0].

docs.title: 12. vsuart_tx_enable_disable_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.4.2.4 Method: Self-check TM Priority: Medium

Verify that clearing UEN[0] aborts transmission and clears TX FIFO.

Pass criteria: Only the character written after re-enabling TX is transmitted (transmitted data = new written data).

docs.title: 13. vsuart_rx_basic_test_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.1.3.2, F2.5.2.1, F2.5.2.3, F2.5.4.1 Method: Self-check TM Priority: High

Verify reception on rx, RX FIFO read via APB and back-to-back reception.

Pass criteria: Read data = data sent on rx, in the same order; no frame is lost; FRERR=0, PRERR=0; RBDSTA=0 after the last read.

docs.title: 14. vsuart_rx_frame_formats_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.5.2.2 Method: Self-check TM Priority: High

Finished date in test plan: 26/10/28; Status: PASS (confirmed by the project owner).

Verify reception in all frame formats (8/9 data bits, none/even/odd parity, 1/2 stop bits).

Pass criteria: PRDATA[7:0] (8-bit mode) or PRDATA[8:0] (9-bit mode) = data sent on rx; FRERR=0, PRERR=0.

docs.title: 15. vsuart_rx_baud_drift_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.5.1.1 Method: Self-check TM Priority: Medium

Verify reception with +-2% baud rate mismatch on rx.

Pass criteria: Read data = data sent on rx for all frames; FRERR=0, PRERR=0.

docs.title: 16. vsuart_rx_enable_disable_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.5.2.4 Method: Self-check TM Priority: Medium

Verify that rx is ignored while UEN[1]=0.

Pass criteria: No data is stored while UEN[1]=0; after re-enabling, read data = data sent on rx.

docs.title: 17. vsuart_rx_fifo_full_overflow_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.5.4.2, F2.5.4.3, F2.5.6.3 Method: Self-check TM Priority: Medium

Verify RX FIFO boundaries, the full interrupt (RXISEL=2'b11) and RX FIFO overflow (RBOSTA).

Pass criteria: Read data = the first 128 characters sent, in order; the 129th character is dropped; RXIFS asserts at 128 stored characters; RBOSTA asserts only on the 129th frame.

docs.title: 18. vsuart_rx_fifo_underflow_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.1.2.2, F2.5.4.4 Method: Self-check TM Priority: Medium

Verify PSLVERR on reading an empty RX FIFO.

Pass criteria: Reading an empty RX FIFO gives PSLVERR=1 and does not change the FIFO; a valid read returns the data sent on rx.

docs.title: 19. vsuart_rx_irq_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.5.6.1, F2.5.6.2 Method: Self-check TM Priority: Medium

Verify RX interrupt generation for RXISEL=2'b0x and 2'b10.

Pass criteria: RXIFS and ifs_rx assert at the RX FIFO level selected by RXISEL (1 or 96 characters) and de-assert after writing 1 to IFS[8].

docs.title: 20. vsuart_rx_error_detect_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.2.2.1, F2.5.3.1, F2.5.3.2 Method: Self-check TM Priority: Medium

Verify framing and parity error detection and read-to-clear of FRERR / PRERR.

Pass criteria: Each invalid frame sets the expected STA error bit and ERRIFS; reading STA clears FRERR/PRERR; writing 1 to IFS[16] clears ERRIFS and ifs_err.

docs.title: 21. vsuart_irq_w1c_clear_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.2.3.1, F2.6.1.1 Method: Self-check TM Priority: Medium

Verify write-1-to-clear of IFS bits and de-assertion of the interrupt pins.

Pass criteria: Writing 1 clears only the selected flag; writing 0 has no effect; each interrupt pin de-asserts after its flag is cleared.

docs.title: 22. vsuart_clock_cdc_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F1.1.1, F1.1.2, F2.4.3, F2.5.5.1 Method: Waveform + Self-check TM Priority: Medium

Verify TX and RX data transfer between PCLK and sys_clk domains for every clock configuration.

Pass criteria: Clock frequencies match 5. Clock Value; transmitted data = written data and read data = data sent on rx, in order, for every clock row.

docs.title: 23. vsuart_full_duplex_test
docs.text:
Covered items: F2.1.3.3 Method: Scoreboard Priority: High

Verify simultaneous transmission and reception with independent data streams.

Pass criteria: Transmitted data = written data and read data = data sent on rx, both in order, without loss; final status shows TX/RX idle and empty FIFOs.
